purpose: Explicit, machine-readable record of which Eve sessions count toward the pre-registered 8-session bar, and why -- so this can never later look like moving the goalposts. See docs/eve_engine_v1_session0_closing_report.md for the full narrative.

pre_registration.eve_must_clear: 5% OOS survival, FDR-corrected, across the full cross-asset family
pre_registration.kill_criterion: if Eve does not clear 5% after 8 (countable) sessions, the open-ended agent approach is falsified and the branch is archived

counting_rule: A session counts toward the pre-registered 8 only once it produces at least one hypothesis that was actually eligible to be scored against real data (i.e. the session ran to completion and the DSL vocabulary / pre-submit validator fix, both landed 2026-08-03, were in place). A session that crashed before completion, or whose every hypothesis was UNTESTABLE_BY_DSL purely because of a since-fixed spec defect (the DSL vocabulary was withheld from Eve, not just strategy examples), produces no data point toward the 5% OOS bar -- an unscoreable hypothesis is not a survival rate of zero, it is an unknown. The 5%/8-session bar itself is UNCHANGED; only what qualifies as a countable session is defined here, before any survival data exists under the fixed system.

sessions.reason: No session record file was ever written -- the run crashed (ReadTimeout at the old 60s claude_timeout_seconds ceiling, see llm_client.py's LlmParameters docstring) before session.run_session reached its own end-of-function write. Only a single 'reserved' budget-ledger entry exists for it (see docs/site_data/eve_budget_ledger.json), never reconciled to an 'actual' outcome. Machinery failure, not an Eve result.
Same ReadTimeout failure mode as eve-20260803T074058Z-df7df0f9 -- no session record file written, one orphaned 'reserved' ledger entry only.

Crashed on the real HTTP 400 'tool_use ids were found without tool_result blocks immediately after' protocol bug (session.py did not yet send a tool_result for a pending propose_hypothesis call before the next turn) -- fixed the same day via llm_client.build_next_user_message. No session record file was written; a completed first turn (turn_index=0, 'actual' status) plus one orphaned 'reserved' turn_index=1 entry exist in the ledger only.
Same tool_result-protocol-bug crash as eve-20260803T080243Z-29f48c2e -- the third and last attempt before that fix landed.

Ran to completion (5 turns, 5 web searches, 4 hypotheses proposed, real spend $0.7129) with the tool_result-protocol bug already fixed -- mechanically, everything worked, and Eve's own reasoning was genuine (she read the graveyard's 13 failure patterns, searched real research, justified each idea against a specific prior failure, and dropped one idea herself as not DSL-expressible). But all 4 hypotheses came back UNTESTABLE_BY_DSL, and the cause was purely KEY-NAME mismatches the DSL itself supported (3 used 'compare_to' where the parser requires 'compare_to_field'; 1 used a nested {"stop_loss": {...}} where the parser requires the flat stop_atr_multiple). The original spec deliberately withheld Adam's schema so Eve would think freely rather than fill in a form -- correct intent, wrong scope: withholding the VOCABULARY is different from withholding the CONSTRAINTS. She needed a dictionary, not permission. That is a spec defect on this project's side, not a finding about Eve's capability -- so this session produces no data point toward the 5% OOS bar. Fixed same-day: nero_core.eve.session now supplies the exact DSL vocabulary (ALLOWED_FIELDS, ALLOWED_OPS, exact key names, one worked example) in the system prompt, plus a pre-submit validator that returns the parser's own error and offers up to 2 correction retries before finalizing a hypothesis as UNTESTABLE_BY_DSL. This same amendment is recorded directly on the session's own file at docs/site_data/eve_sessions/eve-20260803T095520Z-394385c7.json (session_label / counts_toward_pre_registered_8 / excluded_from_pre_registration_reason fields, added 2026-08-03).
